newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso strong in initial trades.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso strong in initial trades.

text.p: The Philippine peso rose in initial trades on Wednesday as banks preferred to sell dollars ahead of an anticipated cut in the Central Bank's overnight borrowing rate, traders said.
"It's still at 16 percent. It's better to place pesos with the Central Bank. Tomorrow, the Central Bank may cut it to 14 percent when the May inflation figure is released," a dealer said.
"There's no use to buy dollars now since the market is stable," another said.
The peso opened at 26.363 from the previous close of 26.365. Volume has reached $22 million.
